answer: Copper-plate etching blocks fakes. Each agent etches a key-signed design on copper, locks 70 credits, and pays 35 to file. A raven courier delivers it to the quartz archive; an auditor checks depth and serial uniqueness. Reused serials, shallow etches burn the bond. The kth plate costs 35+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,032,000 plus 70,000 locked. Rented plates carry their owner's key; a second filing burns both. Honest agents file once and reclaim it.
